content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from officially unveiling a brand-new smart display device. The report also revealed design details of this highly anticipated smart home hub device.

Bloomberg pointed out that this home hub will feature a 6-inch square screen, and the overall design is reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — the latter uses a hemispherical base with a metal stand supporting the screen.

According to Mark Gurman, the thickness of the device is "about the same as an iPhone", with bezels of approximately a quarter-inch in black, similar to older iPads. The corners of the body have been rounded, with "absolutely no sharp edges".

Below are more design details revealed in the report:

  • The body uses Apple's "standard gray aluminum casing", with "rubber material added to the bottom for more stable placement".
  • The device is equipped with a USB-C port for power supply, and has no built-in battery, so it must be connected to power at all times.
  • The bottom features a "circular metal base, equipped with a multi-ring perforated speaker grille".
  • The screen is connected to the base via a "polished metal stand".
  • Users can tilt the screen forward or backward to adjust the angle.
  • The body has no volume buttons or power buttons.
  • The front features a FaceTime camera, and there is no rear camera.

Bloomberg also mentioned another version of the home hub "designed for wall-mounted use". This version is also powered by USB-C, and the base adopts a "slim square design placed below the screen, with built-in speakers and microphones". According to the report, the base "will be mounted against the wall, installed below the screen".

To read the full report, please visit Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to get one (or even several)? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
